solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Here you see what may make crowds so cruel

definitions.text: Here you see what may make crowds so cruel

indicators.note: the clue words can be made into something new by rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: A remark about what turns a crowd vicious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may make' signals rearranging the thirteen letters of 'crowds so cruel'; the whole clue is also a description of itself, a puzzle clue on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The thing you are reading is itself a puzzle clue built from an anagram of those words.

clue.text: Cotton on a reel is in a tangle

indicators.note: a tangle of thread jumbles things, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Thread wound on a spool has become knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cotton' looks like the thread in the scene, but 'Cotton on' is a British idiom meaning to understand; 'in a tangle' rearranges A REEL IS.
explanation.definitionFit: To cotton on is informal British for coming to understand something, which is to grasp it fully.

clue.text: Such pomposity is not a front

definitions.meaning: putting on airs, a superior manner
a flank or edge rather than the face of something

explanation.surface: A remark that someone's self-importance is genuine, not an act.
explanation.definitionFit: Side is dated British slang for pretentious airs, and a side is also a lateral face distinct from the front.

clue.text: Deviously managed to chew up pound notes

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to chew is to gnaw
L is the abbreviation for pound sterling (librae)
E and D are two musical notes

explanation.surface: Someone got through money by chewing up banknotes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the chewing word; 'pound notes' looks like banknotes but splits into a pound sign and two musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle something is to obtain or arrange it by cunning or trickery.

clue.text: They are inclined to support overhead development

definitions.text: They are inclined to support overhead development

parts.words: They are inclined to support overhead development
parts.note: read literally: sloping timbers that hold up a building's roof as it goes up, not people disposed to back a project

explanation.surface: Some people are disposed to back a costly building project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inclined' seems to mean willing and 'overhead' seems to mean business costs; really they are sloping beams and the roof.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloping beams forming the framework of a roof are physically inclined and hold up what is above.

clue.text: It tastes sweet, but schoolboys disliked it

definitions.meaning: the sugar plant whose stalks yield sweetness
the rod once used for corporal punishment in schools

explanation.surface: Something pleasant to taste that pupils nevertheless hated.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar comes from a tall grass of that name, and the same word names the stick used to beat pupils.

clue.text: Out of bed with a jump — he's only just made it

parts.note: someone out of bed is up
a jump or sudden flinch is a start

explanation.surface: Someone leaps out of bed, just in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made it' sounds like arriving on time, but means someone who has only recently risen in status.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart is a person newly risen to importance, often resented as presumptuous.

clue.text: It helps people to get their bearings

definitions.text: It helps people to get their bearings

parts.words: It helps people to get their bearings
parts.note: bearings here are heraldic devices on a shield, granted by an official body, not directions found with a compass

explanation.surface: A guide or map that helps the lost find their way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearings' suggests orientation; in heraldry it means the charges on a coat of arms, which a London institution grants.
explanation.definitionFit: The English body that grants coats of arms is the heraldic authority from which families obtain armorial devices.

clue.text: Policeman's examination paper?

parts.note: not a test sat by a constable but a document authorising officers to inspect premises

explanation.surface: The exam a police officer sits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'examination paper' suggests a test; split it as examination (a search) and paper (a written authority).
explanation.definitionFit: A court order permitting police to inspect a property is a legal document licensing such an inspection.

clue.text: Fellow following Judah's son continuously

indicators.note: the fellow comes after Judah's son, so it is placed second

parts.note: Onan is a son of Judah in Genesis
a don is a fellow of a university college

explanation.surface: A man walking behind a biblical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: A DON is a university teacher, often a Fellow of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means without stopping, going on at length, which is to say continuously.

clue.text: It makes sense if it is used to win at cards

indicators.note: the letters of the clue words are made into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A tip that a tactic is sensible when playing cards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' rearranges SENSE IF; 'It' and 'if it is' are links. In bridge, the term names a play trying to win a trick with a card lower than the opponents' best.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, this is a play that tries to take a trick with a lower card while a higher one is held by an opponent.

clue.text: Put down, face to back

indicators.note: front to back means the word is turned round and read backwards

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Something placed face downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face to back' sounds like laying something face down; it says turn DIAL round.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, meaning set or put down on a surface.

clue.text: Skins reversed to show nap

parts.note: peels are the skins of fruit

explanation.surface: Fruit skins turned over to show the fuzzy surface of fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nap' looks like the pile of a cloth, in keeping with skins, but it is a short sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A nap is a short period of slumber, a brief doze.

clue.text: Blonde and beautiful

explanation.surface: Praise for a golden-haired beauty.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes pale or light hair, and in older usage also means lovely or attractive.

clue.text: Excited by Italian wine — red to start with

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling white wine from Piedmont

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word red is used

explanation.surface: Someone thrilled by Italian wine, starting with a red.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red' looks like a red wine following on; only its first letter is taken.
explanation.definitionFit: Astir means up and about, in a state of excited activity.

clue.text: Ecologically inexperienced

explanation.surface: Someone new to environmental matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The colour word describes environmentalist concerns and also a novice who lacks experience.

clue.text: Fancied one at the party, we hear

indicators.note: says the words are spoken and judged by their sound

parts.note: a guest is someone invited to a party

explanation.surface: Someone took a liking to a person at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancied' looks like 'was attracted to', but means supposed or conjectured.
explanation.definitionFit: To fancy can mean to suppose or imagine, as in 'I fancied it would rain'.

clue.text: Extensive exercise done by prisoners

definitions.meaning: a reaching, lengthening movement of the limbs
slang for a prison sentence served

explanation.surface: A workout carried out by inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a lengthening exercise of the muscles and, in slang, a term of imprisonment.

clue.text: There's nothing to restrict the view

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pinion is to bind or restrain the arms

explanation.surface: Nothing blocks the view from here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the view' seems to mean scenery, but means a point of view.
explanation.definitionFit: One's view on a matter is one's belief or judgement about it.

clue.text: Die, frozen stiff

parts.note: not perishing from cold but a frozen solid shaped like a dice

explanation.surface: A grim instruction or fate: to perish of cold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Die' looks like a verb about death; it is the noun, one of a pair of dice, a cube.
explanation.definitionFit: A small block of frozen water is shaped like a die, a six-faced solid.

clue.text: One of a group knocked down in an alley

definitions.text: One of a group knocked down in an alley

parts.words: One of a group knocked down in an alley
parts.note: not a mugging victim but a skittle in a bowling alley

explanation.surface: A gang member beaten up in a back street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alley' suggests a back street; it is a skittle alley, where a group of pins is knocked down.
explanation.definitionFit: Skittles uses a set of wooden pins arranged in a group and knocked down by a ball.

clue.text: Composer returns script with a neat twist

indicators.note: the abbreviation is sent back, read backwards

parts.note: MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a script

indicators.note: the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A composer sends back a manuscript, neatly altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns MS into SM; 'twist' rearranges A NEAT into ETANA.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedřich Smetana was a 19th-century Czech composer, known for Má vlast.

clue.text: Withdraw with a slight injury

definitions.meaning: to pull out of a race or contest

explanation.surface: Pulling out of an event because of a minor knock.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means to remove a competitor from a race and also a superficial wound such as a graze.

clue.text: Article on a crime explosion in the country

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: an explosion blows the letters apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about a surge in crime across the nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'explosion' rearranges A CRIME into MERICA.
explanation.definitionFit: The United States is commonly called by this name as a nation.

clue.text: A word of agreement, or more than one

definitions.text: A word of agreement, or more than one

parts.words: A word of agreement, or more than one
parts.note: the yes-word of Parliament, put in the plural, also names the votes in favour

explanation.surface: A definition of 'yes', with a nod to many voters.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural of the yes-word also means those voting in favour in a division.
explanation.definitionFit: Each vote of yes is an aye, so several of them, or the voters in favour, are the plural form.

clue.text: Way in for all competitors

definitions.meaning: the field of those entered for a contest

explanation.surface: A doorway for everyone taking part.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means an entrance and also the total number of entrants in a competition.

clue.text: Northern river erosion

definitions.meaning: the river through Durham and Sunderland in north-east England
gradual damage by use or friction

explanation.surface: Erosion along a river in the north.
explanation.definitionFit: The Wear is a river in north-east England, and the common noun means deterioration through use.

clue.text: Raise stake, this mount is hotly tipped

indicators.note: in a down clue, raising a word lifts it bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: an ante is a poker stake put in before the deal

explanation.surface: A poker player raises a bet on a horse tipped to win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Raise stake' and 'hotly tipped' sound like betting; really it is a mountain whose tip is hot.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian volcano is a mountain whose summit is famously hot and active.

clue.text: Register to do work on the farm

definitions.text: to do work on the farm
definitions.meaning: to plough or cultivate the land

explanation.surface: Signing up for farm work.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a cash drawer at a shop counter and also to cultivate soil for crops.

clue.text: Rise to show appreciation

parts.note: to mount an exhibition is to show it
appreciation in value is a rise, an increase, which is up

explanation.surface: Standing up to applaud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appreciation' looks like gratitude, but is the financial sense, a gain in value.
explanation.definitionFit: To increase steadily in amount or build up is to rise.

clue.text: One may set out in it for instruction

indicators.note: the letters are set out, arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A pupil starts out in a course of teaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set' rearranges OUT IN IT; 'One may' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tuition is teaching, the giving of lessons or instruction.

clue.text: Get back to front

parts.note: not reversing something but retaking first place in a race

explanation.surface: An instruction to turn something round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back to front' suggests a reversal; read as 'get back' plus 'to front', it means retake first place.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover first position in a race is to retake the front place after losing it.
